Question: A researcher wants to scale up a reaction one hundred times. Why simply using a proportionally larger flask and proportionally more reagents can lead to unexpected safety issues, even if the original small-scale reaction was safe?

Options:
A. Larger flasks are more prone to breakage
B. Larger quantities always require different safety protocols
C. Scaled-up reactions are inherently more dangerous
D. The surface-to-volume ratio changes, affecting heat transfer
